findings.affected_surface: bin/autopilot.js startup and E4 read-only CLI verification
findings.claim: The planned CLI wiring inherits a filesystem write before the events branch executes, so reader-level checks alone cannot establish the command's read-only guarantee.
findings.evidence: The supplied entrypoint unconditionally calls ensureTmpdir(process.env) before routing commands. The supplied implementation creates a missing configured TMPDIR through ensurePrivateDir. E4 changes the events routing and usage but does not address this startup behavior; its tree digests cover existing repo, live and source directories.
findings.evidence_reference: bin/autopilot.js initial startup block; scripts/lib/runtime-paths.js:ensureTmpdir and ensurePrivateDir; plan E4 steps 1 and readonly-* verification
findings.repair: In E4, ensure the events invocation bypasses directory creation during startup. Add an executable-level test with a nonexistent TMPDIR and verify that the command leaves it nonexistent while returning the required envelope.

findings.affected_surface: E1 warning contract and E2 absent-source handling
findings.claim: The plan explicitly suppresses warnings for missing sources, contradicting the frozen requirement that source problems degrade with a warning.
findings.evidence: KR-A1.3 requires an absent source to produce a warnings entry naming its source and code. E2 step 1 instead specifies ENOENT as state absent with no warning. These prescribe different observable behavior for the same condition.
findings.evidence_reference: Frozen rubric R15; plan KR-A1.3; plan E1 envelope warnings; plan E2 step 1
findings.repair: Resolve the contract before E1 ships: define an absent-source warning code, require an aggregated warning for each missing configured source, and preserve exit 0. Distinguish absent optional discovery candidates from an unavailable source explicitly in the contract and acceptance tests.

findings.affected_surface: E3 cursor.js / merge.js resume filter; KR-A1.2; docs/events-contract.md cursor section
findings.claim: The resume filter as written loses late rows, and KR-A1.2 asks for an ordering that late rows make impossible. The plan says to drop any event with (ts,id) <= (t, last id) OR whose hash is in w. A late row with ts inside [t-SLACK, t) satisfies the first clause, so it is always dropped. That contradicts 'a late row is delivered once, never lost' and resume case (ii). If the OR becomes 'drop only if in w', then w must hold every event already delivered inside the slack window, including events from earlier pages. As specified, w only holds ids from the current page, so earlier-page events inside the window come back as duplicates. Separately, delivering a late row after the watermark cannot match a single full read sorted by (ts,id), so 'the same ordered id list as one full read' cannot hold after an out-of-order append.
findings.evidence: E3 Cursor: 'drops any event with (ts,id) <= (t, last id) or whose hash is in w, and returns the rest. A late row ... is delivered once, never lost.' w = 'id hashes of every returned event whose ts is within SLACK of t'. KR-A1.2: 'gives the same ordered id list as one full read: 0 duplicates, 0 gaps, also after the live JSONL was appended to'. Red-check (b) assumes w rescues the late row, but under an OR it can only drop more.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E3 Cursor bullets 1-2, §2 KR-A1.2, E3 Verify case (ii), E3 red-checks (b)/(c)
findings.repair: Rewrite the filter as: re-read from t-SLACK; drop an event iff its hash is in w, or iff ts < t-SLACK. Define next w as (previous w pruned to ids with ts >= newT-SLACK) union (this page's ids with ts >= newT-SLACK); this needs per-id ts or a stored lower bound, so store w as [hash, ts-offset] pairs. Restate KR-A1.2 as: the union of delivered ids equals the full-read id set with 0 duplicates and 0 gaps; order holds within a page and across pages except for rows that arrived late within SLACK, which are delivered in the next page. Document this in the contract doc before E1 freezes it.

findings.affected_surface: cost.turn id rule (E1 kinds table) vs jsonl-tail offset hints (E2 step 1, E3 h)
findings.claim: The cost.turn id suffix #n is 'the count of earlier byte-identical lines in the file'. That can only be computed by reading the whole file from byte 0. A warm resume starts at a hinted offset and cannot see earlier identical lines. It would assign n=0 to a line that a full read numbers n>=1, so the ids differ between hinted and unhinted reads. That breaks 'deleting h yields the identical event list' and the content-only, stable id guarantee. Ids are part of the frozen /1 contract, so this rule must be fixed before E1.
findings.evidence: Kinds table cost.turn id: 'sha256(raw line)[0:24] + #n, n = count of earlier byte-identical lines in the file'. E3: 'h = per-file offsets ... an optimisation only. Deleting h yields the identical event list'. KR-A1.5: warm resume reads <= 5 % of the cost file bytes.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 kinds table row cost.turn; §4 E2 step 1; §4 E3 Cursor bullet h; §2 KR-A1.5
findings.repair: Pick one rule in E1. (a) Carry a per-file map {line hash -> count seen so far} in the hint, keyed by head hash, and fall back to a full read when it is missing. This keeps n exact but grows the cursor. (b) Define n as the ordinal among identical lines at or after a stable anchor that the hint also carries. (c) Drop #n and collapse byte-identical cost lines as one event, with a documented under-count. Add a red-check case: two identical cost lines, the second appended after a hinted read; hinted and unhinted ids must be equal.

findings.affected_surface: E1 fixture (scripts/lib/events-fixture.js), golden list, check-events-contract.js check (iii), doc examples
findings.claim: The fixture must live in an mkdtemp dir, but several golden ids and envelope fields depend on that random path, so 'hand-computed constants' cannot exist. cost.turn ids hash the raw line, and the raw line includes cwd, which is the tempdir repo path. A decision row without decision_id hashes the canonical row, which includes the stamped repo_identity path. project.repo_identity and project_key are derived from the tempdir realpath. qc.verdict ids are commit shas, which change with author/committer date unless pinned. So the golden-id equality in KR-A1.1 and the doc-examples-equal-fixture gate (iii) are either nondeterministic or force a fixed real path that the tempdir rule forbids.
findings.evidence: E1 Fixture: 'buildFixture({dir}) creates under a tempdir ... returns the golden {kind,id,ts} list as hand-computed constants in the test'. Kinds table: cost.turn id = sha256(raw line); cost rows carry cwd; decision fallback id = sha256(canonical row). Envelope: repo_identity 'git-common-dir:<realpath>'. E4 gate (iii): 'the doc examples equal the fixture's golden events'. §5: tempdir only.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 Fixture, kinds table, Envelope; §4 E4 step 2 (iii); §2 KR-A1.1; §5 first row
findings.repair: In E1, state that the golden list is computed in the test with its own sha256 helper, from the literal row text the test wrote after substituting the tempdir path, never by the code under test. Ids that do not depend on path stay literal constants. Pin GIT_AUTHOR_DATE, GIT_COMMITTER_DATE, name and email in the fixture so commit shas are constant. Normalise doc examples (tempdir to <tmp>, project_key and repo_identity to placeholders) before gate (iii) compares them, and say so in the doc.

findings.affected_surface: E1 ts rule; qc.verdict and dispatch.* readers
findings.claim: The ts rule drops any source timestamp that fails strictIsoMs, and the plan names no normalisation step. The qc reader uses git %cI, which prints strict ISO 8601 with a local offset and second precision (for example 2026-11-02T09:00:00+01:00), not ms+Z. If strictIsoMs requires milliseconds and Z, as its name and the envelope ts format imply, every qc.verdict is dropped as ts_invalid. Shell-written manifest timestamps (date -u in dispatch-hetero.sh) are likely second precision too. KR-A1.1 would then fail for these kinds, or the implementer would quietly diverge from the frozen contract.
findings.evidence: E1 Event bullet: 'A source timestamp that is not a strict ISO instant (same strictIsoMs rule as src/status/decisions-sidecar.js) drops that event with warning ts_invalid; the feed never invents a time.' qc row: git log --format=%H%x1f%cI.... Envelope ts example is millisecond Z. decision-ledger.js writes new Date().toISOString(), which is ms Z, so only decision rows are known to match.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 Event bullets, kinds table rows qc.verdict and dispatch.started; scripts/decision-ledger.js append()
findings.repair: Define the accepted input grammar per source in E1: RFC 3339 instants with Z or a numeric offset, second or finer precision, parsed exactly and normalised to UTC .sssZ. Lenient Date.parse forms are rejected with ts_invalid. Add fixture rows with %cI offset dates and second-precision manifest times, plus one malformed ts, to KR-A1.1 and KR-A1.3.

findings.affected_surface: review.collected / review.finalized id key; decision.row id key; merge.js duplicate_id handling
findings.claim: The review id '<phase>:g<generation>' carries no ledger identity. Two unrelated review ledgers in the same repo that reuse a phase name (two plans each with an E1 phase, re-reviews on different branches) collide. merge then collapses them, keeps one and calls it a bug (duplicate_id), so one review's history is silently lost. The same happens for decision.row when the ledger holds two rows with the same decision_id and kind, which decision-ledger.js allows without --dedupe. Ids are frozen after merge, so changing them later breaks consumers' de-dup.
findings.evidence: Kinds table review.* id '<phase>:g<generation>'; E2 step 4: 'a copy of a live ledger collapses by id <phase>:g<n>'; E3 Merge: 'collapse equal ids (a duplicate id across sources is a bug: keep one, warn duplicate_id)'. decision-ledger.js: --dedupe is optional, so a plain append can repeat kind+decision_id.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 kinds table rows review.collected / decision.row; §4 E2 step 4; §4 E3 Merge; scripts/decision-ledger.js append()
findings.repair: Add a stable ledger discriminator to the review id that an archive copy preserves, for example a ledger id written by collect next to collected_at, or the sha of the first chain entry's base..head. Old ledgers fall back to base+head of entry g1. Decide that repeated decision rows (same decision_id and kind, different ts) are distinct events, keyed for example with a sha256 suffix of the canonical row. Add a fixture case with two ledgers sharing a phase name.

findings.affected_surface: E3 h hints combined with --limit
findings.claim: The plan does not say which offset goes into h when a page is cut by --limit or by the w cap. If a reader stores EOF after a cut, rows past the cut that were read but not returned are skipped on the next hinted read. That gives a gap that 'delete h yields the same list' would expose.
findings.evidence: E3: 'h = per-file offsets keyed by head hash: an optimisation only'; Merge: 'cut at --limit, compute has_more and the next cursor from the last returned event'. Readers return events plus stats with no per-event offset.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E2 reader interface, §4 E3 Cursor and Merge
findings.repair: Specify that each event carries its source byte offset internally. The next h for a file is the smallest of: the start offset of any line not yet delivered, and the start of the first line with ts >= newT-SLACK. Add resume case (ix): pages of 1 with hints equal pages of 1 without hints.

findings.affected_surface: KR-A1.3 vs E2 step 1 (absent source)
findings.claim: KR-A1.3 asks the 'absent' case to produce one warnings[] entry naming source and code. E2 step 1 says ENOENT gives state absent and no warning, and the warning code enum has no absent code. The degrade test cannot satisfy both.
findings.evidence: KR-A1.3: 'absent, empty, unreadable ... exit 0, valid envelope, one warnings[] entry naming source and code'. E2 step 1: 'ENOENT -> state:"absent", no warning'. Envelope codes list has no absent value.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §2 KR-A1.3; §4 E2 step 1; §4 E1 Envelope warnings codes
findings.repair: Pick one rule before the E1 schema. Either absent and empty are reported only via sources[].state, with 0 warnings, and KR-A1.3 says so, or add a source_absent code to the enum.

findings.affected_surface: schemas/events.schema.json enums (warnings[].code, source, sources[].state, ts_basis, row_kind)
findings.claim: /1 is additive-only, but the plan does not say whether enum-like string fields are closed in the schema. If warnings[].code or source is a closed enum, any new code or source later (for example quota.observed, already foreseen in §7 and §8) is a breaking change for a consumer that validates strictly. It is also unclear whether 'ignore unknown fields' covers unknown enum values.
findings.evidence: §2.6: consumers 'pin schema == autopilot.events/1 and ignore unknown fields'. §7 and §8 Q2 foresee a later quota.observed kind 'in /1.1' and call it additive. The envelope lists codes and sources as fixed sets.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §2.6, §4 E1 Envelope/Event, §7, §8 Q2
findings.repair: In the schema and doc, mark kind, warnings[].code, source and row_kind as open sets: consumers must skip unknown kinds and tolerate unknown codes. Define that adding a kind or code is additive under /1. Drop the '/1.1' wording, or define what a minor version means for the pinned schema string.

findings.affected_surface: envelope project.repo_identity; docs/events-contract.md examples; evidence transcripts
findings.claim: The envelope always carries repo_identity 'git-common-dir:<realpath>', which is an absolute path that normally sits under the home directory. It goes to the hangar console and any downstream fleet surface. The plan's own leak test ('greps the golden envelope for home/tmp path') would trip on it. The 'Not exposed on purpose' list omits it.
findings.evidence: Envelope: "repo_identity": "git-common-dir:<realpath>". §6 Risks: 'a test greps the golden envelope for home/tmp path and token patterns'. E4 step 6 scrubs paths only in the evidence transcript.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 Envelope, §6 risk row 'Secrets, prompts or home paths leak', §4 E4 step 6
findings.repair: Expose only project_key, plus an optional repo basename, in the envelope. Keep repo_identity internal for filtering, or behind an explicit --debug flag outside the contract. Make the leak grep in the test cover the full envelope.

findings.affected_surface: consumer table (C1 open/blocked/done, G1 QC), qc.verdict, decision.row
findings.claim: The consumer table has C1 derive open/blocked/done from dispatch.started/ended. A dead-pid run never gets an ended event, so it shows as open forever. That is inferring liveness from the absence of a record, while the plan itself says liveness is the watcher's job. Separately, qc.verdict (a commit trailer a model can write) and decision.row kinds such as unknown (documented in decision-ledger.js as 'a claim') reach G1 and A4 with no flag separating self-reported from observed.
findings.evidence: Kinds table dispatch.ended: 'A running or dead-pid manifest yields no ended event (liveness is the watcher's job)'. Consumer table C1: dispatch.started/ended 'for open/blocked/done'. decision-ledger.js header: 'unknown ... (agent self-report — a claim, S6)'.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 kinds table and consumer table; scripts/decision-ledger.js header
findings.repair: In the consumer table, state that the absence of dispatch.ended means 'not ended', not 'running', and that C1 gets liveness from 'autopilot status runs'. Add data.basis 'observed|self_reported' (additive) to qc.verdict and decision.row: git trailers and agent-written rows are self_reported. State in the doc that G1 must not render self_reported values as verified state.

findings.affected_surface: cross-host transport of autopilot.events/1 to hangar console
findings.claim: §7 says each host serves its own feed and the console merges by project_key and host, but the plan never says how a remote host's feed reaches the console. If it travels courier to hub, the shape must come from contracts/ to gen/, and F1's single hub change must already carry it, either as an opaque payload or as a generated type. Freezing /1 here without that check risks a second hub contract change.
findings.evidence: §7: 'Cross-host aggregation (each host serves its own project feed; the console merges by project_key and host)'. No contracts/ or gen/ file appears in the §3 file map.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §7 bullet 5, §3 file map
findings.repair: Add one line to §0 or §7. Either: the feed is read only locally (the console or courier on each host runs the command) and crosses the hub only inside an F1-defined opaque envelope. Or: list the contracts/ entry and confirm F1 already covers it.

findings.affected_surface: cost.js project filter (cwd -> git common dir)
findings.claim: Cost rows are kept only while their cwd still resolves to the project's git common dir. A vanished cwd counts as rows_filtered. Dispatch worktrees are routinely removed, so once one is reaped its cost rows silently leave the feed. A cold read later then returns fewer cost.turn events than an earlier warm read did, and C1 'cost today' under-reports. History becomes non-deterministic over time, and the per-source foreign-row fixture does not cover this.
findings.evidence: E2 step 2: 'Project filter by cwd -> git rev-parse --git-common-dir, memoised; a vanished cwd counts as rows_filtered.'
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E2 step 2, §6 risk row on host-wide sources
findings.repair: For a vanished cwd, fall back to a prefix match against the project's worktree paths, including git worktree list and paths recorded in manifests' worktree field. Otherwise emit a cwd_unresolved warning with a count, so the loss is visible. Add a fixture row whose worktree was removed.

findings.affected_surface: qc.js git log --since window
findings.claim: The qc reader limits git log with --since=<sinceTs - slack> on committer date. A commit that becomes reachable later with an older committer date is never returned, for example a fast-forward or merge of commits made on another clone, or a branch created before the watermark and merged after. git's date limiting can also stop traversal early when clocks are skewed. The plan never names this as out of contract.
findings.evidence: E2 step 5: '--since=<sinceTs - slack> when a window exists'. qc row: ts = committer date; --branches HEAD.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E2 step 5, kinds table row qc.verdict
findings.repair: Either document qc.verdict late arrival as out of contract, or drop --since and instead bound by commit count or by a per-branch tip hint stored in h (rev-list old-tip..new-tip), ordering by committer date. Add a resume case that merges an old-dated commit after the watermark.

findings.affected_surface: bin/autopilot.js entry, KR-A1.6 read-only claim, --project flag
findings.claim: bin/autopilot.js calls runtime-paths.ensureTmpdir at startup, before any subcommand. It creates TMPDIR (mkdir 0700) when TMPDIR is set but missing, so 'autopilot status events' is not strictly write-free, and the readonly-* digest does not look at TMPDIR. Separately, --project <project_key> cannot be served for a repo other than cwd: the git-common-dir sources (decision ledgers, work-orders, git log) need a repo path, and a 16-hex key cannot be turned back into one.
findings.evidence: bin/autopilot.js top block: require('../scripts/lib/runtime-paths').ensureTmpdir(process.env). runtime-paths.js ensureTmpdir -> ensurePrivateDir -> mkdirSync when TMPDIR is set and absent. E1: '--project: default = project of cwd'.
findings.evidence_reference: bin/autopilot.js lines 5-8; scripts/lib/runtime-paths.js ensureTmpdir/evaluateTmpdir; plan §4 E1 The command, §2 KR-A1.6
findings.repair: Scope KR-A1.6 explicitly: the CLI entry may create a missing TMPDIR, and the events module writes nothing. Or skip the ensure step for 'status events'. Add a readonly case with TMPDIR set but absent. Restrict --project to the cwd's own key (any other key is a usage error, exit 2), or define a key-to-repo lookup.

findings.affected_surface: scripts/status-events.test.js environment isolation
findings.claim: The sandbox list sets HOME, TMPDIR, AUTOPILOT_COSTS_FILE, AUTOPILOT_DISPATCH_RUNS_DIR and AUTOPILOT_CONFIG_FILE. It does not clear AUTOPILOT_EVENTS_REVIEW_LEDGERS, the live-dir variable, AUTOPILOT_ROOT_RUN_ID, or the GIT_* and global git config, so a developer's shell can leak real stores into tests. The mode-000 and chmod a-w cases pass vacuously or fail when tests run as root, which is common in containers. A module-level git rev-parse memo is process-global state shared across in-process tests.
findings.evidence: §5 row 1 env list; E2 step 4 reads env AUTOPILOT_EVENTS_REVIEW_LEDGERS; KR-A1.3 mode 000; KR-A1.6 chmod a-w; E2 step 2 'memoised'.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §5, §4 E2 steps 2 and 4, §2 KR-A1.3/KR-A1.6
findings.repair: Build the test env from an explicit allowlist, not by copying process.env. Set GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL to a tempdir file. Pass ctx.env everywhere. Scope the memo per collectEvents call. Skip permission cases with a logged reason when getuid() is 0.

findings.affected_surface: docs/events-contract.md placement vs repo-layout rule 7; §8 Q1 pointer writer
findings.claim: repo-layout rule 7 (active from P1) flags any docs/*.md outside docs/guide or docs/dev. findings.evidence_reference: scripts/lib/repo-layout.js DEFAULT_REGISTRY.rules id 7; plan §3, §2.6, §4 E2 step 4, §8 Q1
findings.repair: Register events_contract_doc at docs/dev/events-contract.md now, or add a per-file exception with a reason. Fold the Q1 pointer into §2.6 (an additive writer change), §3, E2 step 4 and one hetero-review-loop.test.sh assertion, with a red-check.

findings.affected_surface: free-text data fields (decision.rationale, qc subject/verdict, run.stage reason)
findings.claim: Free text from model-written sources (decision rationale up to 240 chars, commit subject up to 120, run.stage reason) is exposed verbatim. 'autopilot status events --json' is also run from agent shells. The plan caps the text but has no runtime redaction, and its token-pattern grep only covers the fixture's golden envelope. A credential pasted into a rationale or commit subject would reach a model's view and the console.
findings.evidence: Kinds table: rationale? (<= 240 chars), subject (<= 120 chars), reason? (<= 120 chars). §6: 'a test greps the golden envelope for home/tmp path and token patterns'. §8 Q3 exposes rationale.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E1 kinds table, §6 risk row on secrets, §8 Q3
findings.repair: Apply a deterministic redaction pass (common token and key patterns replaced with [redacted]) to every free-text field at read time, and count redactions in sources[]. Add a degrade or fixture case with a token-shaped rationale.

findings.affected_surface: schemas/events.schema.json validated by scripts/validate-json-schema.js

backlog_candidates.affected_surface: cross-host transport of autopilot.events/1 to hangar console
backlog_candidates.claim: §7 says each host serves its own feed and the console merges by project_key and host, but the plan never says how a remote host's feed reaches the console. If it travels courier to hub, the shape must come from contracts/ to gen/, and F1's single hub change must already carry it, either as an opaque payload or as a generated type. Freezing /1 here without that check risks a second hub contract change.

backlog_candidates.affected_surface: cost.js project filter (cwd -> git common dir)
backlog_candidates.claim: Cost rows are kept only while their cwd still resolves to the project's git common dir. A vanished cwd counts as rows_filtered. Dispatch worktrees are routinely removed, so once one is reaped its cost rows silently leave the feed. A cold read later then returns fewer cost.turn events than an earlier warm read did, and C1 'cost today' under-reports. History becomes non-deterministic over time, and the per-source foreign-row fixture does not cover this.
backlog_candidates.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E2 step 2, §6 risk row on host-wide sources

backlog_candidates.claim: The qc reader limits git log with --since=<sinceTs - slack> on committer date. A commit that becomes reachable later with an older committer date is never returned, for example a fast-forward or merge of commits made on another clone, or a branch created before the watermark and merged after. git's date limiting can also stop traversal early when clocks are skewed. The plan never names this as out of contract.
backlog_candidates.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-11-02-oc-a1-events-contract.md §4 E2 step 5, kinds table row qc.verdict

backlog_candidates.affected_surface: bin/autopilot.js entry, KR-A1.6 read-only claim, --project flag
backlog_candidates.claim: bin/autopilot.js calls runtime-paths.ensureTmpdir at startup, before any subcommand. It creates TMPDIR (mkdir 0700) when TMPDIR is set but missing, so 'autopilot status events' is not strictly write-free, and the readonly-* digest does not look at TMPDIR. Separately, --project <project_key> cannot be served for a repo other than cwd: the git-common-dir sources (decision ledgers, work-orders, git log) need a repo path, and a 16-hex key cannot be turned back into one.
backlog_candidates.evidence_reference: bin/autopilot.js lines 5-8; scripts/lib/runtime-paths.js ensureTmpdir/evaluateTmpdir; plan §4 E1 The command, §2 KR-A1.6

backlog_candidates.claim: The sandbox list sets HOME, TMPDIR, AUTOPILOT_COSTS_FILE, AUTOPILOT_DISPATCH_RUNS_DIR and AUTOPILOT_CONFIG_FILE. It does not clear AUTOPILOT_EVENTS_REVIEW_LEDGERS, the live-dir variable, AUTOPILOT_ROOT_RUN_ID, or the GIT_* and global git config, so a developer's shell can leak real stores into tests. The mode-000 and chmod a-w cases pass vacuously or fail when tests run as root, which is common in containers. A module-level git rev-parse memo is process-global state shared across in-process tests.

backlog_candidates.affected_surface: docs/events-contract.md placement vs repo-layout rule 7; §8 Q1 pointer writer
backlog_candidates.claim: repo-layout rule 7 (active from P1) flags any docs/*.md outside docs/guide or docs/dev. A new docs/events-contract.md will fail layout-lint as soon as the in-flight relayout reaches P1. Separately, §8 Q1 decides that collect writes a ledger pointer under <git-common-dir>/autopilot/, but E2 step 4, the §2.6 compatibility list, the §3 file map and the tests do not include it.

backlog_candidates.affected_surface: free-text data fields (decision.rationale, qc subject/verdict, run.stage reason)
backlog_candidates.claim: Free text from model-written sources (decision rationale up to 240 chars, commit subject up to 120, run.stage reason) is exposed verbatim. 'autopilot status events --json' is also run from agent shells. The plan caps the text but has no runtime redaction, and its token-pattern grep only covers the fixture's golden envelope. A credential pasted into a rationale or commit subject would reach a model's view and the console.
